"'''He Wasn't Man Enough'''" is a song by American singer [[Toni Braxton]]. It was written by [[Rodney "Darkchild" Jerkins]], [[Fred Jerkins III]], [[LaShawn Daniels]], and [[Harvey Mason, Jr.]] for her third studio album, ''[[The Heat (Toni Braxton album)|The Heat]]'' (2000), while production was helmed by the former. "He Wasn't Man Enough" is an uptempo R&B song that differs from Braxton's previous [[Sentimental ballad|ballads]]. The song was released by [[LaFace Records]] on February 29, 2000, as the [[Single (music)|lead single]] from the album.

The song received generally positive reviews from music critics, many of whom praised it as one of Braxton's best works.<ref name="allmusic1">{{cite web|last=Thomas |first=Stephen |url=https://www.allmusic.com/album/r473144/review |title=The Heat - Toni Braxton |publisher=AllMusic |date=April 25, 2000 |access-date=February 20, 2012}}</ref> "He Wasn't Man Enough" had international success and became one of Braxton's signature songs, peaking at number two on the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]], where the single stood for several weeks, and number one on the [[Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs|Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Singles & Tracks]] chart for four weeks. As of 2025, this song is her last solo top 10 appearance on the ''Billboard'' Hot 100. An accompanying [[music video]] was released for the single. The song earned Braxton her fourth [[Grammy Award for Best Female R&B Vocal Performance]] and was nominated for [[Best R&B Song]] in [[43rd Grammy Awards|2001]].

"He Wasn't Man Enough" is a song by American singer Toni Braxton. It was written by Rodney "Darkchild" Jerkins, Fred Jerkins III, LaShawn Daniels, and Harvey Mason, Jr. for her third studio album, The Heat (2000), while production was helmed by the former. "He Wasn't Man Enough" is an uptempo R&B song that differs from Braxton's previous ballads. The song was released by LaFace Records on February 29, 2000, as the lead single from the album.

The song received generally positive reviews from music critics, many of whom praised it as one of Braxton's best works. "He Wasn't Man Enough" had international success and became one of Braxton's signature songs, peaking at number two on the Billboard Hot 100, where the single stood for several weeks, and number one on the Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Singles & Tracks chart for four weeks. As of 2025, this song is her last solo top 10 appearance on the Billboard Hot 100. An accompanying music video was released for the single. The song earned Braxton her fourth Grammy Award for Best Female R&B Vocal Performance and was nominated for Best R&B Song in 2001.

sections.heading: Background and composition
sections.wikitext:
"He Wasn't Man Enough" was released as the lead single from [[Toni Braxton]]'s third studio album, ''[[The Heat (Toni Braxton album)|The Heat]]''. The song was written by [[Rodney Jerkins]], [[Fred Jerkins III]], [[LaShawn Daniels]], and [[The Underdogs (duo)|Harvey Mason, Jr.]], while it was produced by Jerkins. The song was recorded in the United States during the production of Braxton's third studio album, between January and February 2000.<ref>{{cite magazine| url=https://ew.com/article/2000/01/24/latest-toni-braxtons-new-album/ | magazine=Entertainment Weekly | first=Tom | last=Sinclair | title='Heat' Seeker | date=January 14, 2000}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine| url=https://ew.com/article/2000/01/05/britney-spears-plots-janet-jackson-move/ | magazine=Entertainment Weekly | first=Craig | last=Seymour | title=Nasty Girl | date=January 5, 2000}}</ref> During its production, L.A. Reid said "It's very strong, and very personal to her".<ref>{{cite magazine|last1=Sinclair|first1=Tom |title=The latest on Toni Braxton's new album|url=https://ew.com/article/2000/01/24/latest-toni-braxtons-new-album/|magazine=Entertainment Weekly|access-date=August 11, 2017|date=January 24, 2000}}</ref>

All instruments on "He Wasn't Man Enough" are played by Jerkins and the background vocals are sung by Braxton, Nora Payne, Sharlotte Gibson, and Jerkins.<ref name="heatnotes">{{cite AV media notes|title=The Heat|title-link=The Heat (Toni Braxton album)|year=2000|type=US CD album booklet|publisher=[[LaFace Records]], [[Arista Records]]|id=73008-26069-2}}</ref> The song was recorded in a key signature of [[E minor]]. [[Popmatters]] praised Braxton, saying "the track seems to be an attempt to make some headway within the lucrative urban R&B market."<ref name="popmatters1">{{cite web|last=Ross |first=Colin |url=https://www.popmatters.com/pm/review/braxtontoni-heat |title=Toni Braxton: The Heat < PopMatters |publisher=Popmatters.com |access-date=February 20, 2012}}</ref>

The song earned Braxton her sixth [[Grammy Award for Best Female R&B Vocal Performance]] in [[43rd Grammy Awards|2001]].<ref>{{cite magazine |last=Taylor |first=Chuck |date=October 19, 2002 |title=Braxton is back with 'More' |magazine=Billboard |page=9 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Hw0EAAAAMBAJ&pg=PA9 |access-date=August 11, 2017}}</ref> According to ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard.com]]'', this song is her last Top 10 appearance on the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] to date.
sections.text:
"He Wasn't Man Enough" was released as the lead single from Toni Braxton's third studio album, The Heat. The song was written by Rodney Jerkins, Fred Jerkins III, LaShawn Daniels, and Harvey Mason, Jr., while it was produced by Jerkins. The song was recorded in the United States during the production of Braxton's third studio album, between January and February 2000. During its production, L.A. Reid said "It's very strong, and very personal to her".

All instruments on "He Wasn't Man Enough" are played by Jerkins and the background vocals are sung by Braxton, Nora Payne, Sharlotte Gibson, and Jerkins. The song was recorded in a key signature of E minor. Popmatters praised Braxton, saying "the track seems to be an attempt to make some headway within the lucrative urban R&B market."

The song earned Braxton her sixth Grammy Award for Best Female R&B Vocal Performance in 2001. According to Billboard.com, this song is her last Top 10 appearance on the Billboard Hot 100 to date.

sections.heading: Critical reception
sections.wikitext: "He Wasn't Man Enough" was widely acclaimed by contemporary music critics. Stephen Thomas Erlewine from [[AllMusic]] highlighted the track along with "Gimme Some" as having a "skimmering beat".<ref name="allmusic1"/> David Browne from ''[[Entertainment Weekly]]'' gave it a positive review, certificating it with a B rating. He said "From producer Rodney Jerkins' cushiony pulse to its premise (one woman warning another about her ex-beau), the amenable single "He Wasn't Man Enough" sounds mightily familiar. But it's still no "Scrubs", largely thanks to Braxton's husky, mumbly delivery."<ref>{{cite magazine| url=https://ew.com/article/2000/03/31/he-wasnt-man-enough/ | magazine=Entertainment Weekly | title=Music Review: He Wasn't Man Enough, by Toni Braxton|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131212080054/https://www.ew.com/ew/article/0,,276094,00.html|url-status=live|archive-date=December 12, 2013}}</ref> ''[[NME]]'' gave it a positive review, saying that for the track, "Braxton can probably claim the best set of tonsils in soul-pop".<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.nme.com/reviews/toni-braxton/3164 |title=NME Track Reviews - He Wasn't Man Enough |publisher=Nme.Com |date=April 1, 2000 |access-date=February 20, 2012}}</ref> ''[[Rolling Stone]]'' ranked the song number 17 on its list of "The 100 Greatest R&B Songs of the 21st Century".<ref>Rolling Stone ranked the song No. 17 on its "The 100 Greatest R&B Songs of the 21st Century".</ref>{{full citation needed|date=May 2025}}

sections.heading: Chart performance
sections.wikitext: "He Wasn't Man Enough" peaked at number two on the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] for two weeks in May 2000, becoming Braxton's sixth and last top-10 single. The song spent 37 weeks on the chart. The song also peaked at number one on the [[Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs|Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Singles & Tracks]] chart for four weeks. The song debuted at number five on the [[UK Singles Chart]] on its issue date of April 29, 2000. The song debuted at number six on the [[Australian Singles Chart]] and peaked at number five in that country. The song debuted at number 36 on the [[New Zealand Singles Chart]] and later rose to number five after seven weeks on the charts. The song received [[platinum certification|platinum]] by the [[Recording Industry Association of New Zealand]] (RIANZ), selling over 15,000 copies there.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.rianz.org.nz/rianz/chart.asp?chartNum=1230&chartKind=S |title=The Official New Zealand Music Chart |publisher=Rianz.org.nz |access-date=February 20, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120422181624/http://rianz.org.nz/rianz/chart.asp?chartNum=1230&chartKind=S |archive-date=April 22, 2012 |url-status=dead }}</ref> The song debuted at number 99 on the [[French Singles Chart]] before falling out, then re-entering at number 74 on the charts and eventually peaked at number fifteen, becoming the biggest jump of the issue date of July 1, 2000. The song debuted at number 21 on the [[Single Top 100]], peaked at number five and stayed on the charts for seventeen weeks.<ref>{{cite web|title=Toni Braxton - He Wasn't Man Enough |url=http://www.dutchcharts.nl/showitem.asp?interpret=Toni+Braxton&titel=He+Wasn%27t+Man+Enough&cat=s|website=Dutch Charts|access-date=August 11, 2017}}</ref>
sections.text: "He Wasn't Man Enough" peaked at number two on the Billboard Hot 100 for two weeks in May 2000, becoming Braxton's sixth and last top-10 single. The song spent 37 weeks on the chart. The song also peaked at number one on the Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Singles & Tracks chart for four weeks. The song debuted at number five on the UK Singles Chart on its issue date of April 29, 2000. The song debuted at number six on the Australian Singles Chart and peaked at number five in that country. The song debuted at number 36 on the New Zealand Singles Chart and later rose to number five after seven weeks on the charts. The song received platinum by the Recording Industry Association of New Zealand (RIANZ), selling over 15,000 copies there. The song debuted at number 99 on the French Singles Chart before falling out, then re-entering at number 74 on the charts and eventually peaked at number fifteen, becoming the biggest jump of the issue date of July 1, 2000. The song debuted at number 21 on the Single Top 100, peaked at number five and stayed on the charts for seventeen weeks.

sections.heading: Music video
sections.wikitext:
The music video, directed by [[Bille Woodruff]] from February 25–26, 2000,<ref name="nydailynews">{{cite news |last1=Fink |first1=Mitchell |last2=Rubin |first2=Lauren |url=http://articles.nydailynews.com/2000-02-29/gossip/18133933_1_bmg-michael-dornemann-clive-davis |work=[[New York Daily News]] |title=Actor Has Too Familiar A Ring For Robin Givens |date=February 29, 2000 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110815042450/http://articles.nydailynews.com/2000-02-29/gossip/18133933_1_bmg-michael-dornemann-clive-davis |archive-date=August 15, 2011}}</ref> begins with Braxton as an animated [[superhero]] who unzips her shirt to ward off villains. Next, she is shown dancing in a red cylinder-like hallway. The shot turns to a club where her ex (portrayed by Braxton's former husband Keri Lewis of R&B group [[Mint Condition]]) and his current wife (portrayed by [[Robin Givens]]) walk in. Givens looks Braxton up and down and flashes her [[wedding ring]] at her. Braxton scoffs as she knows of his infidelity.

The video flashes between Braxton dancing in the hallway and the club scene. At one point, the two women are in the club's bathroom, and Braxton informs the new wife why she dumped her husband. They set up an act, wherein Braxton goes into a private room with him and gets him to drop his pants; all the while he is on camera, and everyone at the club, including his current wife, is watching. At the end, Givens busts in and throws the ring at him, and the two women give each other a high five.

The video also features cameo appearances by [[Rodney Chester]] and Braxton's sister [[Tamar Braxton|Tamar]]. Originally cast to play the husband, actor [[Michael Jai White]] ended up dropping out before the video shoot because Givens allegedly took issue with White resembling her former husband [[Mike Tyson]], whom White played in the HBO film ''[[Tyson (1995 film)|Tyson]]'' five years earlier.<ref name="nydailynews"/><ref>{{cite web|last=Farber|first=Jim|title=SOFT AND SEXY Toni Braxton has a new album, a new video and a 'cute' new man. How sad is that?|url=http://www.nydailynews.com/soft-sexy-toni-braxton-new-album-new-video-cute-new-man-sad-article-1.876907|work=New York Daily News|date=April 23, 2000|access-date=March 31, 2018}}</ref> He would appear in the video for Braxton's "[[Hands Tied]]" a decade later.

The music video, directed by Bille Woodruff from February 25–26, 2000, begins with Braxton as an animated superhero who unzips her shirt to ward off villains. Next, she is shown dancing in a red cylinder-like hallway. The shot turns to a club where her ex (portrayed by Braxton's former husband Keri Lewis of R&B group Mint Condition) and his current wife (portrayed by Robin Givens) walk in. Givens looks Braxton up and down and flashes her wedding ring at her. Braxton scoffs as she knows of his infidelity.

The video flashes between Braxton dancing in the hallway and the club scene. At one point, the two women are in the club's bathroom, and Braxton informs the new wife why she dumped her husband. They set up an act, wherein Braxton goes into a private room with him and gets him to drop his pants; all the while he is on camera, and everyone at the club, including his current wife, is watching. At the end, Givens busts in and throws the ring at him, and the two women give each other a high five.

The video also features cameo appearances by Rodney Chester and Braxton's sister Tamar. Originally cast to play the husband, actor Michael Jai White ended up dropping out before the video shoot because Givens allegedly took issue with White resembling her former husband Mike Tyson, whom White played in the HBO film Tyson five years earlier. He would appear in the video for Braxton's "Hands Tied" a decade later.
